messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@brightlane.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-12T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: POC observed prefetch stall during long context test

Hi Monica / Marissa,

Quick note from our POC run this morning. When we exercised a ~12k token context with repeated prefix prompts the SDK session stalled mid-stream twice; client saw no new tokens for ~7s before completion. We attached a trimmed trace from our client (brightlane_prefetch_trace.txt).

What we observed:
- Works fine on shorter contexts (<=4k tokens).
- On the long context, server returned intermittent 429-ish/timeout metadata in logs, but final output still rendered.
- We do see a prefetch configuration in the SDK set to "aggressive" (we used your default sample).

This is blocking our latency SLA estimate for the BrightLane product — can we get eyes from your runtime team? We need an ETA on root cause and whether a config change or code fix is required.

Thanks,
Ellen
Product Lead, BrightLane AI

Attachment: brightlane_prefetch_trace.txt (text/plain, 28KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-12T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: ACTION: triage BrightLane POC prefetch stall (info + repro)

Team — quick handoff: BrightLane hit a reproducible stall when using our JS SDK with an "aggressive" prefetch profile against a long (>10k tokens) context. Ellen attached a trimmed client trace. Key asks:

1) Can runtime reproduce with the same SDK sample? SDK details from Ellen: JS SDK v2.3.1, default prefetch=aggressive, request size: messages + 12k token prompt, streaming=true.
2) If reproducible, is this a scheduling/batching edge case (continuous batching + large KV cache) or an SDK-side prefetch bug?
3) If it's runtime, can we provide a temporary config shim (reduce prefetch window) for BrightLane while we patch?

Deliverables:
- Quick triage note by EOD (tomorrow 3/13) with repro steps and a temp mitigation we can offer the customer.
- If confirm runtime bug -> patch ETA and whether a hotfix is feasible within 72h.

I'll coordinate customer comms once you have the triage note.

Thanks — please reply inline with status.

Monica

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-12T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: triage BrightLane POC prefetch stall (info + repro)

Quick update after an initial pass in staging:

- I pulled the trace and replayed the request shape against our staging cluster using the same SDK config (v2.3.1). I can reproduce a pause in token emission around the 9k–11k token window when streaming=true and prefetch=aggressive.
- The runtime logs show a burst of KV cache compaction and a CPU spike on the broker process right before the pause. No explicit 5xx from model process, but gRPC streams saw transient flow-control backpressure.

Open questions:
- Is the SDK prefetch handler sending overlapping fetches that can cause duplicate cache writes? Karthik, can you confirm whether the JS prefetch implementation in v2.3.1 uses idempotent cache tokens or might race on busty contexts?
- I can try toggling prefetch to "conservative" to confirm whether it's a config mitigation. If that reduces stalls, we can suggest that as a short-term fix.

I'll attach a short trimmed runtime log and a minimal repro script in a follow-up once Karthik confirms SDK internals.

-Dev

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-13T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: triage BrightLane POC prefetch stall (info + repro)

Thanks Dev — quick confirm from SDK side: v2.3.1 prefetch is single-writer, but aggressive mode does pipeline fetch windows that can overlap when context windows are large and latency to the broker fluctuates. We do have a guard, but it only dedups identical request ids — not overlapping sequence ranges.

Immediate repro/mitigation notes:
- Reproduce locally with the attached minimal repro (I reproduced Dev's pause).
- Temp mitigation: set prefetch="conservative" or reduce windowSize from 4 to 2 for BrightLane test runs. That avoids the overlapping pipeline and removed the pause in my runs.
- Long-term: SDK change to dedupe overlapping sequence ranges or add a per-session prefetch mutex. I can put up a PR for SDK v2.3.2 with the mutex and a changelog entry.

I'll open PR and coordinate a small runtime gating test. If runtime team can confirm that reduced prefetch avoids the KV compaction spike, we can offer config change + SDK patch.

Karthik
Senior SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC observed prefetch stall during long context test

Ellen — update from our triage: short version: we reproduced and have a safe interim mitigation plus a planned SDK patch.

What happened: our runtime team saw overlapping prefetch windows in the aggressive SDK profile that, under some broker latency patterns, caused a transient KV compaction burst and a short pause in token streaming.

What we can do now (immediate):
- Please switch your POC runs to prefetch=conservative or set windowSize=2 in the SDK. This should remove the stall while we push a code fix.
- If you want, we can remotely flip that config for your POC instance for the next 24–48h while you validate.

Planned fixes:
- SDK PR (v2.3.2) from Karthik with a per-session prefetch mutex and dedupe for overlapping ranges. Target: in review by 3/17, publish by 3/20.
- Runtime follow-up: small broker-side guard to smooth KV compaction under overlapping prefetch; tentative hotfix branch available if needed (Dev can provide patch).

Attachments: runtime_hotfix.patch (if you'd like a server-side quick test) and our POC checklist (poc_requirements.xlsx).

Next steps:
- Ellen: confirm whether you want us to flip the config remotely for your test window or if you'll change the SDK config and re-run.
- Monica/Marissa: I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk through the mitigations with BrightLane.

Thanks — appreciate the quick repro help.

Monica Patel
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
